steps.name: Slum Dweller
steps.text: Thank you, Dr. Gavial.

steps.name: Slum Dweller
steps.text: I feel a little better now.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Sorry... This is all I can do.

steps.name: Slum Dweller
steps.text: It's okay. Not like there's a cure for Oripathy. Every day I live is a bonus.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I'm new in town. Is there a doctor here who's knowledgeable about Oripathy?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Slum Dweller
steps.text: Well, a Sarkaz doctor came here a few months ago and bought out some ruins on the west end.

steps.name: Slum Dweller
steps.text: She told people she had candy that could cure Oripathy.

steps.name: Slum Dweller
steps.text: She handed it out in exchange for a test tube's worth of blood.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: People believed that?

steps.name: Slum Dweller
steps.text: Not in the beginning, but some were desperate enough to send their children there. When the children actually started getting better, people started to believe.

steps.name: Slum Dweller
steps.text: Normally, that would have been the end of the story...

steps.name: Slum Dweller
steps.text: But there have been rumors in the slums about a missing child.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Missing... you think that doctor did it?

steps.name: Slum Dweller
steps.text: The last person who saw the kid said she went to the doctor.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Why didn't anyone confront her?

steps.name: Slum Dweller
steps.text: We're afraid... Those who have been to that place say it's full of blood bags.

steps.name: Slum Dweller
steps.text: She's a nasty character, too. Feels like she could start killing people any time.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Why not report her to the lord ameer?

steps.name: Slum Dweller
steps.text: ...The nobility couldn't care less about a homeless child gone missing.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I'll go, then.

steps.name: Slum Dweller
steps.text: Are you really going?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I want to see if that doctor can really treat Oripathy.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: If she's a fake who's been kidnapping children... she'll get what's coming to her.
The room is so decrepit that Gavial thought she had come to the wrong place at first.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: No, there's a smell...

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: This is...

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: The smell of blood.
She takes one step forward and kicks something.
She looks down.
It is a shoe, without a doubt that of a child.
There is a pool of dried blood next to it.
She feels the hairs on the back of her neck stand up.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: What happened here?
She bends down and sniffs the blood.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: This is real blood, alright.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Did a kid really die here?
She notices a candy next to the pool of blood.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Is this the candy that the doctor's handing out?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: It's... a plain old ordinary candy.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Tricking kids with candy, huh...

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Who's there?
Gavial looks up to see a girl standing at the top of the stairs, staring down at her.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Hey, kiddo. Can you tell me what happened here?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Wait!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Hmph—

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Just what is going on here?
You again?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Wait!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: No need to be scared! I'm here to help you!
...I see.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Are you the doctor who lives here?
Gavial has no time to be surprised at the blood bags hanging everywhere, for there is a Sarkaz with white hair and red eyes standing in front of her.
A Vampire. She remembers reading about them in a book.
A tribe of the Sarkaz, as powerful as they are infamous.
They walk in shadows, feeding upon the blood of others. There is no murder they will not commit, no evil they will not stoop to...

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Y—You're a Vampire?!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I get it now. You use candy to lure children here so you can feed on them!

steps.name: Evil Vampire
steps.text: And who might you be?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I'm Gavial. Doctor Gavial. I'm here to expose your evil plot!

steps.name: Evil Vampire
steps.text: I don't have time for you right now. Sleep.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: What... did you... do to me...?

steps.name: Evil Vampire
steps.text: Just fiddled with your blood circulation.

steps.name: Evil Vampire
steps.text: Be a good girl and nap for a while.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I... I feel like I'm burning...

steps.name: Evil Vampire
steps.text: You're still standing after being hit by my Arts.

steps.name: Evil Vampire
steps.text: Intriguing.

steps.name: Evil Vampire
steps.text: Who are you?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I said... my name... is Gavial...

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: That's... Doctor... Gavial...

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I came to save this girl—argh!

steps.name: Evil Vampire
steps.text: You broke free. Most intriguing...

steps.name: Evil Vampire
steps.text: Most intriguing indeed.

steps.name: Evil Vampire
steps.text: What I wouldn't give for your blood—

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Let her go?

steps.name: Evil Vampire
steps.text: As you wish.
The Vampire's hand brushes against top of the girl's head, and she immediately loses consciousness, collapsing by the Vampire's feet.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: What did you do to her?!

steps.name: Evil Vampire
steps.text: I'm saving her for dinner. Don't worry, she won't feel any pain.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: You... you monster!

steps.name: Evil Vampire
steps.text: If you want to save her, we can make a trade.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: A trade?

steps.name: Evil Vampire
steps.text: Yes. You let me draw your blood in her stead, and I'll let her go. How about that?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Sure.

steps.name: Evil Vampire
steps.text: That was fast.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: She might get hurt if I fought you right here.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: But you'd better keep your promise and let her go.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Otherwise, I won't ever forgive you, even if I die here today!

steps.name: Evil Vampire
steps.text: How do you plan on not forgiving me when you're about to die?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: The tribe shaman says that when the heroes of Acahualla die, their souls go back to Acahualla's lakes.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: 'My soul shall be cleansed by the lake and become the wind in the trees, the rain in the sky.'

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: It's you who should be afraid, Vampire scum.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: You'll remember me when the wind brushes against your face and the rain falls upon your shoulders!

steps.name: Evil Vampire
steps.text: The tribes of Sargon have such delightful traditions.

steps.name: Evil Vampire
steps.text: But you don't understand the Vampires.

steps.name: Evil Vampire
steps.text: The wind is averted by the smell of blood, and the rain turns to blood that nourishes me.

steps.name: Evil Vampire
steps.text: Your soul won't harm me in the slightest.
Seething with rage, Gavial closes her eyes, ready to meet her death.
Before she left the jungle, Gavial thought the most glaring thing that existed was the sun.
Once, she mustered the courage to stare directly at the sun, and it burned her eyes, leaving her seeing double for days.
She thought there could be nothing more glaring that the sun.
She realized she was wrong when she left the jungle.
The most glaring thing is the eyes of other people, staring at the Originium crystals on her body.
She was not afraid of the malice in those eyes, but they are always averted when she tries to look into them.
It took some time for her to learn that her illness was known as 'Oripathy', rather than 'Stone Disease'. And people like her were known as 'Infected'.
She learned that Oripathy was considered incurable.
She learned that most Infected lead hard lives.
In the jungle, there was no such distinction, no discrimination against those afflicted by Oripathy.
She did not understand why. All she knew was that she might be able to make the lives of Oripathy patients better, even if it could never be cured.
So she searched for doctors who claimed to be able to treat Oripathy, trying to learn from them.
But she found only disappointment.
Some were mere frauds. Others were worse, using the treatment of Oripathy patients as a cover for criminal activity.
When she pointed it out, they framed her and made her a fugitive.
Why?
She feels the pain of a needle going into her arm, then the feeling of loss as her blood is drawn.
Her friends in Acahualla do not even know what happened to her.
She should have gone back to see them, just once.
The sense of loss is soon gone.
Then, silence.
Is this death?
Do Vampires kill painlessly?
No. She is still alive!

steps.name: Evil Vampire
steps.text: Your blood is surprisingly healthy, despite the high concentration of Originium crystals.

steps.name: Evil Vampire
steps.text: I knew it. You really are a remarkable physical specimen.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: You're not going to kill me?

steps.name: Evil Vampire
steps.text: Why would I kill you? I said let me draw your blood in her stead.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: But... you're a Vampire, aren't you...? Isn't drawing blood the same as killing?

steps.name: Evil Vampire
steps.text: Some of my kind like to do that, but I'm not interested.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Why do you do it, then?

steps.name: Evil Vampire
steps.text: You freed yourself from my Arts by sheer willpower. I'm very interested in your blood.

steps.name: Evil Vampire
steps.text: But fighting you would be quite bothersome, so I improvised.

steps.name: Evil Vampire
steps.text: Thank you for your cooperation.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Who are you?

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: You may call me Warfarin. Doctor Warfarin.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Wake up, kiddo.

steps.name: Infected Girl
steps.text: Mm... hm?

steps.name: Infected Girl
steps.text: Did you come to get treated too?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I came looking for you.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Everyone thought you went missing.

steps.name: Infected Girl
steps.text: I didn't.

steps.name: Infected Girl
steps.text: The doctor told me I was too weak and needed to rest, so I didn't go out.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: So... you weren't tricking them with candy?

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Some people wouldn't even believe that a Vampire could become a doctor. You can't convince these people to believe something that exceeds their capacity for imagination.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: You don't try to clear things up?

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: I stopped caring about how people felt centuries ago.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: I would rather spend my time studying blood.

steps.name: Infected Girl
steps.text: Thank you, doctor. I feel much better.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: You give me blood, I give you medicine. Give and take, that's all.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Now run along home. I have research to do, and I don't want to be bothered.

steps.name: Infected Girl
steps.text: Alright! Bye, doctor!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Wait, the candy—

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Yes, it's just ordinary candy.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: But if the patient believes it will work, then it will work.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: We call that a 'placebo'.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: But it's lying, isn't it?

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Can you give them medicine that works?

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: There is no cure for Oripathy. No reason to not lie, if it helps the patient live a little longer.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: The ultimate aim of treatment is to mitigate the patient's suffering. Never mind lying; I would gladly become a demon, if that's what it took for the treatment.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Not that I expect you to understand.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Now begone, and don't bother me again.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I see! That makes so much sense!

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: What? You believe it?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Of course! It makes perfect sense.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Unless you're still tricking me?

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: ...I'm telling the truth. Not many would believe it.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Why? You're absolutely right.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Doctors can't make miracles. I don't care if the patient hates my guts, as long as they get better.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: ...I didn't expect you to be so understanding.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Dr. Warfarin! No, Master Warfarin! I've been searching for a doctor like you, someone who can really teach me how to heal!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Can you teach me about medicine?

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: It's not every day that I meet someone who understands me like this. I suppose I could teach you a thing or two about medicine.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: But I don't want my blood research interrupted.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: You're interested in my blood, right?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: You can take my blood! Study it all you want!

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Well, I've already drawn plenty for my purposes.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Anything troubling you? I could help you take care of it.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Now that you mention it... there is one thing.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: A lack of samples.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: At the end of the day, only a number of simpletons would believe this blood-for-candy thing.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: There are still many Infected who don't trust me.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Besides, you said that rumors about me have started to spread, making it even less likely that people will come.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Before you came, I was planning to make my identity known, and go door-to-door to scare the inhabitants into giving blood.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: You don't think it's a good idea?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Well, I think it's a little too slow.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Even counting me, it's no small task to draw blood from so many people with just the two of us.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: You have a point.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: ...Aha!

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Leave it to me, Master.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Will you train me in medicine if I solve your problem?

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Certainly.
A few days later...

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Gavial hasn't been back for a few days.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Did she run into some sort of trouble?

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: I would have taught her medicine, even if she didn't solve my problem.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Maybe I should go and find her.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Master Warfarin!

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: What took you so long?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Here.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Care to explain all the blood bags?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Well, I do some volunteer medical work in the slums, which means the people there are willing to hear me out.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: They were willing to give their blood when I told them you needed it for their research.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Oh, and I cleared up the rumors about you while I was at it.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Is this enough for your research?

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Plenty.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I've also logged the records, following the sample that you gave me for reference.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Here's the logbook.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: ...Very good. Very good indeed.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Will you train me in medicine now?

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: I never thought I would encounter a woman who's not only after my own heart, but one who can also do the things I can't.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: If only I had met you earlier! I would never have had to worry a lack of samples.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: You can count on me!

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: I've made up my mind, Gavial.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Let's travel together and study the blood of Oripathy patients in different places.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: You'll collect the blood, and I'll study it.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: I'll teach you everything about medicine that I know.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Awesome!
Where exactly do you think you are going, Warfarin?

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: K—Kal'tsit?!

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: How did you find this place?!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I had already zeroed in on this area as your likely hiding spot.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Then I heard about a doctor talking about another Vampire doctor treating patients.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Let's just say it wasn't hard.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: I forgot how well-connected you are.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You've been away from your post for three months.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: I mean, I've been sending back my research reports on a monthly basis! It's not like I've been doing nothing.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: There are certain things that require your physical presence.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It's time for you to come back.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Who are you?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: My name is Kal'tsit, Warfarin's colleague. I'm here to bring her back. What about you?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I'm Gavial. Doctor Gavial!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Warfarin said she'd train me in medicine if I helped her.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Are you taking her away? But we were just about to set out—

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Yes! Gavial and I were about to set out on a journey!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Construction has begun on the blood bank that you requested. You said you wanted to supervise it personally, didn't you?

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: What?!

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: You should have told me earlier! I would have gone back so long ago!

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Looks like our travel plans are going on hold, Gavial.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: B—But what do I do?

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Sorry...

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: What is this place you two are talking about?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It's called Rhodes Island. It's a pharmaceutical company dedicated to the treatment of Oripathy.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Are there a lot of people like Warfarin who can teach me more about medicine there?!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Can I come with you if Warfarin's going back?

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Now there's an idea. This one's a special talent, Kal'tsit, I guarantee it.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Did you collect all these blood bags by yourself?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This logbook...

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Hey, when did that end up in your hands?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Let me see... very detailed data, accompanied by appropriate comments and summaries.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: There is an entrance test you'll have to take, but you'll quality for a clerical position on the strength of this logbook alone.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: But I want to learn medicine!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You'll have no shortage of opportunities if you come to Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Before that, though, I have a question for you.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Why do you want to join Rhodes Island?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Because I want to cure everyone of Oripathy!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Welcome aboard, Gavial.
